prompts.text: What's something people frequently assume you enjoy that you actually don't?
Describe a moment when being honest about a preference improved an outing.
Be understood through a long conversation or through someone noticing your everyday routines?
I suggest an activity everyone else loves but you don't. How would you want to tell me?
People sometimes follow social expectations even when those expectations don't suit their personalities.
Saying what you dislike can help somebody know you as much as listing your favourites.
Which part of your personality usually emerges only after you've spent time with someone?
Recall a person who made you feel comfortable admitting an unpopular preference.
We are choosing a restaurant and neither of us wants to disappoint the other. What question would make it easier?
Discuss our deal-breakers for an outing or the small details that make one enjoyable?
What have your closest friendships taught you about who you feel comfortable around?
Tell me about getting to know a friend's friend and finding an unexpected connection.
Understand why someone keeps a small inner circle or how they maintain several different friendships?
Our social circles overlap for the first time at a gathering. What would make the introductions relaxed?
People can behave differently in a group without being less genuine in private.
You don't need to be best friends with someone's entire circle to build a respectful connection.
How do you notice when a person feels excluded from a group conversation?
Recall someone introducing you thoughtfully when you knew nobody in the room.
We attend an event where one of us knows everyone and the other knows nobody. How could we look after each other?
Spend an evening with a few close friends or meet a wider circle at a casual event?
How were you taught to talk about money while growing up?
Describe the first time you had to plan the cost of an outing for yourself.
Discuss practical spending habits early or wait until a shared expense makes the conversation relevant?
We're considering an activity with very different price options. What's the easiest way to share our budgets?
People often attach different emotional meanings to the same amount of money.
Money compatibility begins with honest expectations, not identical incomes.
What's a purchase you value because of the story behind it rather than its price?
Recall choosing a simple experience over a more expensive plan and being pleased with the result.
I suggest splitting a bill differently from what you expected. How would you want us to discuss it?
Choose an inexpensive recurring tradition or save for one special shared experience?
What does being spiritually or philosophically grounded mean in your everyday life?
Tell me about a moment your beliefs helped you make a difficult decision.
Understand someone's guiding values through stories or through the questions they ask themselves?
We have different religious or philosophical backgrounds. What would make those differences safe to discuss?
A person's convictions may show through daily choices more than formal labels.
Respecting someone else's faith or worldview doesn't require pretending that differences don't matter.
Which value from your upbringing have you kept even as other beliefs have changed?
Recall learning why a celebration or spiritual practice mattered to someone close to you.
I ask how an important belief shapes your plans. How would you prefer to explain it?
Explore the influence of faith on family traditions or the role of personal reflection in decision-making?
What's a small act of consideration that has more meaning to you than other people might expect?
Describe someone remembering how you like to receive support and responding accordingly.
A person who asks before making plans for you or one who knows enough to suggest a suitable option?
We've had very different days and want different things from our evening. How would you negotiate that?
Acts of care are interpreted through personal histories as well as present circumstances.
The right gesture is the one the recipient appreciates, not the one that photographs best.
What do you do when you want to show appreciation but words feel insufficient?
Recall a time somebody's ordinary helpfulness made a lasting impression on you.
I want to acknowledge something important you've achieved without making a big public event of it. What would you prefer?
Receive a thoughtful note or have someone quietly handle an errand for you?
What helps you make a decision when several options are genuinely attractive?
Tell me about changing your mind after hearing an unfamiliar point of view.
Make a decision by comparing practical consequences or by thinking through how each option aligns with your values?
We want opposite weekend plans and have only one free day together. How should we approach a compromise?
People reveal their priorities in the trade-offs they're prepared to make.
Knowing how someone handles uncertainty is as useful as knowing their ambitions.
What's a decision you prefer to make slowly even when others move quickly?
Recall somebody supporting you through a decision without trying to choose for you.
An opportunity arises that affects both our schedules. What questions should come before an answer?
Discuss a difficult choice as it unfolds or revisit it after each person has thought privately?
Which experiences have made you more patient with other people's mistakes?
Describe a conversation where somebody accepted correction with more grace than you expected.
Talk about lessons from a mistake or the habits that help us avoid repeating it?
One of us forgets an arrangement that mattered to the other. How would we repair the situation?
People differ in whether they want a quick apology or a conversation about what happened.
The point of apologising is to take responsibility, not to end the discussion as fast as possible.
How do you prefer someone to tell you when you've disappointed them?
Recall being forgiven in a way that encouraged you to change your behaviour.
Our plans fall through because of a preventable misunderstanding. What would rebuilding trust look like?
Explain what went wrong immediately or set a time to discuss it when both people are calmer?
What is one skill you want to keep learning even if it never earns you money?
Tell me about discovering an interest that surprised people who thought they knew you.
Develop a creative hobby together or learn two different skills and exchange what we discover?
You get a scholarship to spend a month studying anything you like. What topic would you choose?
People can share curiosity even when they have no overlap in their technical interests.
A fulfilling interest doesn't need an audience to be worthwhile.
What kind of environment makes you eager to learn something difficult?
Recall a teacher or mentor whose approach changed how you thought about learning.
We take a class together and one person progresses much faster. What would make the experience enjoyable for both?
Visit an interactive exhibition or attend a small workshop led by a local expert?
What's a normal day in your future life that you'd be excited to experience?
Describe an ordinary moment that helped you realise your priorities had changed.
Imagine the home routines you'd want in ten years or the relationships you'd hope to maintain?
We imagine living in entirely different places later in life. What would make those visions worth discussing?
The day-to-day details of a future can be more revealing than its biggest milestones.
Shared direction matters more than matching every detail of an imagined future.
Which everyday responsibility do you hope to have more control over as you grow older?
Recall seeing someone build a peaceful routine and wondering what choices made it possible.
We're asked to describe an ideal weekday without mentioning our jobs. What would you include?
Explore what stability means to us or discuss how much change makes life interesting?
What's a question you would want to revisit after we've known each other for another year?
Tell me about a person whose character you understood more clearly after seeing them through change.
Look back on the beliefs we began with or talk about the new perspectives we've gained?
Our first impressions of each other turn out to have been incomplete. What might be amusing to compare?
People can surprise each other without having hidden anything about themselves.
Getting to know somebody is an ongoing process, not a checklist to finish.
What would make you feel our conversations are becoming more honest as we get comfortable?
Recall an early conversation whose meaning changed after you learnt more about the person.
We realise an old assumption has shaped how we've spoken to each other. How might we question it kindly?
Keep exploring our differences or focus on understanding the values we have in common?
